newsitem.title: USA: H.J. Heinz lost $230 million in quarter due to restructuring.
newsitem.headline: H.J. Heinz lost $230 million in quarter due to restructuring.

text.p: H. J. Heinz Co., the ketchup maker and owner of Weight Watchers, Tuesday reported a loss of nearly $230 million in the latest quarter, reflecting the impact of restructuring costs.

The company lost $229.5 million, or 61 cents a share, on sales of $2.44 billion in its fiscal fourth quarter ended April 30, vs. year-earlier earnings of $170.2 million, or 45 cents a share, on sales of $2.53 billion.
The Pittsburgh-based company reported pre-tax restructuring charges of $647.2 million, which it expects will help it deliver double-digit earnings growth into the next century.
Excluding the charges, Heinz said it would have earned $186.2 million, or 50 cents a share, in the quarter.

For the year, Heinz reported earnings of $301.9 million, or 81 cents a share, on sales of $9.35 billion, which was down from the previous year's profits of $659.3 million, or $1.75 a share, on sales of $9.11 billion.

"It has now been three months since we presented our ambitious restructuring plans, and I am pleased to say that many of these initiatives are well under way, said Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Anthony J. F. O'Reilly.

"We have signed a definitive purchase agreement with McCain Foods to sell Ore-Ida's foodservice frozen foods business and five factories for approximately $500 million as part of our continuing efforts to dispose of non-strategic businesses," he said.
O'Reilly also said that the company plans to sell or close an additional 10 factories around the world.
Heinz's stock was up 62.5 cents at $46.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
